drafted.title: Unvalidated malformed input processing across agent tool and inference endpoints
drafted.description: An attacker supplies malformed, out-of-range, or unexpectedly-typed data to an agent-adjacent surface — an MCP tool parameter, workflow/flow-node config, model-serving request field, or uploaded file — that the receiving component fails to validate for type, bounds, format, or origin before acting on it. Because agents and inference pipelines chain these components together and routinely forward untrusted user or tool output as input to the next hop, a single missing validation check can cascade into denial of service, memory corruption, path traversal, injection, authentication/authorization bypass, or remote code execution anywhere along the chain.

drafted.title: XML external entity (XXE) injection via unhardened parsers in agent tool pipelines
drafted.description: An agent tool, document loader, or RAG ingestion component parses attacker-influenced XML (uploaded documents, SVG/Office files, SAML/SOAP payloads, tool call results) using a parser that resolves DOCTYPE-declared external entities, letting a crafted entity read local files, trigger SSRF against internal/cloud-metadata endpoints, or exhaust memory via entity expansion. Because agents routinely pipe untrusted external content straight into these library calls as part of normal tool use, a single unhardened dependency in the toolchain becomes a disclosure or pivot primitive the agent unknowingly executes on the attacker's behalf.

drafted.title: Unsanitized agent/LLM output injected into downstream interpreters
drafted.description: Agent frameworks and MCP tool servers frequently splice untrusted input—user prompts, retrieved documents, or LLM-generated text—directly into shell commands, database/graph queries (SQL/Cypher), template engines (Jinja2), eval'd code, or config manifests without escaping or validating special elements. Because the agent's tool layer treats this composed string as trusted, attacker-controlled content can alter the syntax of the downstream interpreter, yielding remote code execution, data exfiltration, or privilege escalation across dozens of otherwise-unrelated agent and MCP products.

drafted.title: Open redirect via unvalidated redirect/callback URL parameter
drafted.description: A login, OAuth/SAML callback, webhook, or MCP-registry endpoint accepts an attacker-controlled URL (via a redirect/return_to/redirectUri-style parameter) and forwards the user or agent's browser/HTTP client to it without validating the destination against an allowlist of trusted hosts. Because the initial link still points at the trusted agent platform, attackers weaponize it to phish credentials, steal OAuth authorization codes/tokens or session identifiers mid-flow, or redirect automated agent/tool traffic to an attacker-controlled server that then returns malicious content or captures secrets.

drafted.title: Cross-origin tool invocation via missing Origin/Host validation on local MCP servers
drafted.description: A locally-bound MCP/agent HTTP server trusts any request that reaches its socket without validating the Origin or Host header, so a malicious webpage opened in the victim's browser (via simple cross-origin requests or WebSocket/SSE connections) or an attacker using DNS rebinding against the loopback address can silently reach the server's API and invoke privileged tools, read secrets, or trigger code execution as the logged-in user. Because the server relies on network binding (localhost-only) rather than verifying the request's claimed origin/host, the 'same-machine' trust assumption is trivially bypassed from any page the victim visits.

drafted.title: Path traversal in tool/model-serving endpoints via unsanitized file path parameters
drafted.description: An agent-adjacent service (model loader, log viewer, extension installer, archive extractor, or MCP-style file tool) accepts a file path, filename, or archive entry name as a tool/API parameter and uses it directly in filesystem operations without canonicalizing or rejecting '../' and '..\' sequences, letting an attacker escape the intended directory. This is routinely chained into arbitrary file read/write/overwrite of configs or extensions, which in turn yields remote code execution in LLM webui, model-registry, and tool-serving frameworks.

drafted.title: Unsandboxed eval injection via attacker-controlled expressions or tool-call arguments
drafted.description: Agent frameworks, workflow builders, and MCP-adjacent platforms often route user-supplied text, workflow expressions, or model-generated tool-call arguments into a language-level eval()/exec() (or an equivalent dynamic code-evaluation path such as a 'sandboxed' expression engine, YAML loader, or custom-code node) without adequately neutralizing control characters or restricting the evaluation context. An attacker who controls any of these inputs — a chat message, a workflow parameter, an LLM-emitted tool argument, or a config field — can inject arbitrary expressions that execute as code, typically yielding full remote code execution on the host running the agent, bypassing whatever sandbox the platform claims to provide.

drafted.title: Arbitrary file read/write via relative path traversal in tool file parameters
drafted.description: An agent-exposed tool or API endpoint (file upload, workflow save/load, profile/personality folder, package edit, media-tag fetch, etc.) accepts a filename or path argument and concatenates it into a filesystem operation without canonicalizing and constraining it to an intended base directory, so an attacker embeds '../' sequences or absolute/symlinked paths to escape the sandbox and read or write arbitrary files on the host. Because the path argument is just another tool-call parameter, it is reachable both from direct API/tool invocation and from untrusted content an agent is tricked into passing through, letting the attacker exfiltrate secrets, corrupt configs, or plant files that achieve remote code execution.

drafted.title: Unrestricted file upload via agent ingestion tool enabling remote code execution
drafted.description: An agent-adjacent platform exposes a file-upload or attachment-ingestion capability (e.g., a 'send file to AI' tool, knowledge-base/media-pool import, or chat attachment handler) that fails to properly validate file extension, MIME type, or content against a strict allow-list. An attacker uploads a disguised executable (web shell, .phar, script with spoofed extension) into a web-accessible or interpreter-reachable path, which is then invoked by the server or a downstream tool-call, yielding full remote code execution on the host running the agent.

drafted.title: Prototype pollution via unsanitized key merge in agent tooling and dependencies
drafted.description: Agent platforms, workflow engines, and the JS libraries they depend on often merge, clone, or path-assign user- or tool-controlled object keys (e.g. `__proto__`, `constructor.prototype`) without sanitization, letting an attacker inject keys that pollute the shared Object.prototype. Because the polluted prototype is global, this silently corrupts unrelated logic across the process — disabling input validation, escaping VM/sandbox isolation in expression or code-execution nodes, tampering with HTTP responses, or ultimately achieving arbitrary code execution in the agent's runtime.
